title: Constructing Innovative Gardens
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Build a sack garden with a stone column in the middle, or a horizontal tyre or bottle garden, from local and reused materials.

skills.key_step: The child tells a vertical garden (grows upwards: sack, stacked tyres, hanging bottles, pockets on a wall) from a horizontal garden (spread flat: tyres laid flat, raised boxes, keyhole bed) and says both save land and water.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the practices in growing vegetables.
floor.question: Name a practice in growing vegetables.

representations: a model sack and a tray garden
steps: Look at the direction it grows.

board.do: Draw a tall sack with plants on its sides.

misconceptions.ask: Which kind of garden needs the least ground?
misconceptions.repair: Stand a sack on the ground and measure the ground it covers.

misconceptions.ask: A sack garden is which kind of garden?
misconceptions.repair: Stand a sack up and lay a tray flat and name each one.

misconceptions.ask: Who can use a sack garden?
misconceptions.repair: Ask where a village school with rocky ground could grow kale.

misconceptions.ask: Old tyres laid flat on the ground and filled with soil make which garden?
misconceptions.repair: Lay a tyre flat and one stacked in a tower; ask which grows upwards.

checks.question: Is a sack garden vertical or horizontal?
Why do people use vertical gardens?

skills.key_step: The child says how an innovative garden is built (a sack or container with drainage holes, a central stone column for water in a sack, soil mixed with manure, planted at the top and sides) and which crops suit it (kale, spinach, onions, herbs, not maize or cassava).

floor.question: What type is a sack garden?

representations: a sack, stones, a tin with both ends cut
steps: Fold the sack edge; place a tin in the middle.
Fill the tin with stones and around it soil with manure; lift the tin.
Make holes in the sides; plant seedlings.

board.do: Draw a sack cut open with a column of stones.
Ask what the stones are for.

misconceptions.ask: Which crop suits a sack garden?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how deep the roots of maize and cassava go compared with kale.

misconceptions.ask: Why is a column of stones placed in the middle of a sack garden?
misconceptions.repair: Pour water into one sack with a column and one without, then open them.

misconceptions.ask: How often does a sack garden need water?
misconceptions.repair: Feel the soil of a sack garden two days after watering.

listen_for: In deep shade behind a wall
misconceptions.ask: Where should a sack garden be placed?
misconceptions.repair: Grow kale in one sack in shade and one in sun for three weeks.

checks.question: Name a crop that suits a sack garden.
Why does a sack garden need a stone column?
checks.answer: so water reaches all the soil
